title: Geometric integrality of an algebra can be tested on finite field extensions
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $S$ a commutative unital $k$-algebra. For a field extension $L/k$ [def-pc-field-extension], write $S\otimes_k L$ for the tensor product of the underlying $k$-vector spaces, with multiplication $(s\otimes a)(t\otimes b)=st\otimes ab$ and unit $1\otimes1$. An integral domain means a nonzero commutative ring in which $uv=0$ implies $u=0$ or $v=0$. If $S\otimes_k L$ is an integral domain for every finite field extension $L/k$ (finite means finite-dimensional as a $k$-vector space), then $S\otimes_k K$ is an integral domain for every field extension $K/k$. No finite-generation or Noetherian hypothesis on $S$ is imposed.
